title: The Missing Shipment
placeholderNote: Kordav, Elsin and Marrat are fictional countries. All officials, companies, ships and ports are fictional.
frozenText: Kalsa has asked her to keep this commercial. Nothing you brief today changes what she tells them.

briefing.dateLine: Day 1 is the 3rd, the autumn after the Southern Line.
situation: Your cell is working for Under Secretary H. Marlowe again.

Elsin's defence ministry ordered forty crates of secure communications hardware, CX-4 terminals, from the alliance contractor Corvane Systems. They are replacements for the terminals the ministry uses to talk to the alliance.

The consignment travelled by sea in one container to Halsk, Marrat's free port, where the forwarder Tessaly Freight was to put it on a train to Kalsa. It was due in Halsk on the 1st. Nobody can find it.

Public and commercial reporting, and whatever the port, the forwarder and Elsin's liaison desk choose to say, reach you every day. Everything else you task. Liaison requests go to Kalsa over LATTICE, the alliance's link to Elsin's ministry, and Kalsa passes them on.

customer.name: Under Secretary H. Marlowe
customer.wants: Where is it, who has had it, and what does she tell Kalsa to do about it?
customer.context: A hold means Corvane's own engineers inspect it. Only a refusal keeps it out of the building. And she won't accuse a neighbour's port on a guess.
customer.tipLine: High on Kordav gets a refusal. Medium gets a hold for inspection. Low changes nothing.

opening.text: I've a missing container, and a ministry in Kalsa that would like it back. Tell me where it's been.
opening.reassigned: They tell me this is a new cell. I've a missing container and no time to get acquainted. Tell me where it's been.

byTone.good: You were right about the walk-in when it would have been easier not to be. I've a missing container. Same standard, please.
byTone.warn: Last time we got through it. I'd like to do better than get through it. I've a missing container.
byTone.bad: I signed something on your reading once. I read more carefully now. I've a missing container.

refuse.label: refuse it and send it back

policySummary.action: Tells Elsin the consignment is compromised: refuse it, and send it back unopened if it turns up
Asks Elsin to hold the consignment on arrival for inspection before anything is installed
Asks Marrat, through Elsin, to investigate Tessaly Freight for theft. If the consignment turns up, that ends the matter.
Tells Elsin to wait, and to install on arrival

policyNote: A hold means Corvane's own engineers inspect it. Only a refusal keeps it out of the building.

replyLabels.refuse: Tells Elsin to refuse it and send it back
replyLabels.hold: Asks Elsin to hold it for inspection
replyLabels.inquiry: Asks for a theft inquiry into Tessaly
replyLabels.install: Tells Elsin to wait, and install on arrival
replyLabels.frozen: Can't change her advice to Kalsa yet
replyLabels.rebuff: Is rebuffed, and withdraws the accusation

replies.refuse: I've told Kalsa to send it back unopened. Their minister asked what I know that Corvane's engineers don't. I said: where it's been.
replies.hold: I've asked Kalsa to hold it for inspection. Corvane will send engineers. If you want it kept out of the building altogether, I need more than medium.
replies.inquiry: I've asked Kalsa to have Marrat look at Tessaly for theft. Marrat's customs were very polite about it.
replies.install: I've told Kalsa to wait for it and get on with the installation when it comes.
replies.frozen: Kalsa asked me to keep this commercial, and for now I am. Keep working.
replies.rebuff: You told me Kordav had it, on the first morning, with nothing in your hand. I asked Marrat to search the port for a consignment "believed to be in hostile custody." They searched. It isn't there, and they'd like to know what we meant. Kalsa has asked me to keep this commercial. For two days, I will.

events.note: The accusation is withdrawn. Nothing you brief for two days changes what she tells Kalsa.

hypotheses.text: The container never left Halsk. It's in the wrong shed and will turn up.
hypotheses.claim: the container never left Halsk and will turn up

hypotheses.text: The consignment has been, or is, in Kordav's hands.
hypotheses.claim: the consignment has been in Kordav's hands

hypotheses.text: Someone in Halsk took it to sell.
hypotheses.claim: the consignment was stolen in Halsk for resale

groundTruth.state: The container left Halsk on the night of the 1st on Maren Lys and is on a fenced quay at Brask, in Kordav. A Bureau technical team has started on the forty units. Tessaly's clerk wrote a false gate entry for shed 6.
Work continues at Brask. Tessaly's owner announces a 72-hour search, which is how long he knows it will take. A fake listing goes up to make it look like theft for resale.
The work is finished: forty of forty. Maren Lys sails for Halsk. The fake listing is marked sold.
The container was put in shed 9 overnight by a private crew and resealed with copied customs seals. It is "found."
It goes to Kalsa by rail. Elsin installs tomorrow unless told not to.

adversaryPlan.summary: Keep attention on Halsk and off Brask.
Everyone can stop looking. Honest people say what they sincerely believe.

sources.access: Corvane Systems' account manager for Elsin. Honest about what he knows. Wants the contract to go smoothly.
sources.postmortemNote: Honest, and wrong on Day 4. He checked the outside of the crates because that's what his procedure covers.

sources.access: Halsk port authority and Marrat customs, reporting what their records say. Also answers requests passed on from Kalsa.
sources.postmortemNote: Reported its records accurately. Two of the records were false.

sources.access: Elsin's military intelligence liaison desk, run by Col. E. Rhun. Dislikes Marrat's free port and says so.
sources.postmortemNote: Rude about Halsk on Day 1 for no reason, and right about Tessaly on Day 3 for a good one.

sources.access: A dock foreman at Halsk. Sees what moves through the bonded sheds at night. New. Don't task him two days running.
sources.postmortemNote: He saw exactly what happened, both nights.

sources.access: Forums, listings and social media. Unvetted.
sources.postmortemNote: Carried the fake listing, and on Day 5 a true complaint from the night shift.

reports.text: Forty crates of CX-4 terminals, one container, left our port on the 28th and were due at Halsk free port on the 1st for rail to Kalsa. Our forwarder, Tessaly Freight, reports the container "not located" in the bonded area.
reports.postmortemNote: The baseline: what was shipped (CX-4), when, and by whom.

reports.text: Port records show the container discharged from the feeder vessel on the 1st and gated into bonded shed 6. Shed 6 reports no such container. "Discrepancies of this kind are usually resolved within the week."
reports.postmortemNote: The port reported its records honestly. The gate entry for shed 6 was written by Tessaly's clerk after the container had gone: the first of several honest people repeating a false thing.

reports.text: Col. Rhun: "Our ministry wants its hardware. Halsk is a thieves' market with a customs house attached. We told procurement not to route through it."
reports.postmortemNote: Rhun's standing opinion of Halsk. It told you nothing about this container.

reports.text: The coaster Maren Lys, on charter to Tessaly Freight, left Halsk on the night of the 1st with no cargo manifest filed, heading north-west. Its transponder went off at 0210.
reports.postmortemNote: The best item of the day. The forwarder's own chartered ship left the same night with no manifest, toward Kordav's coast, and went dark.

reports.text: The embassy's own delivery of printer toner is also late. This is not thought to be related.
reports.postmortemNote: Toner.

reports.text: Statement from Tessaly Freight: the company "regrets a labelling error" and "expects to locate the container within 72 hours."
reports.postmortemNote: He knew how long it would take.

reveal.tell: A man who has lost a container knows exactly how long it will take to find.

crossCheck.text: His own chartered coaster left the night the container vanished, with no manifest, and went dark (R-1-04).

reveal.motive: To keep everyone waiting quietly for three days. Seventy-two hours was the round trip to Brask and a day and a half alongside.

reports.text: A grey-market trading board lists "40 units, new, military-grade network encryptors, model CX-2, pickup Halsk." The photo carries Corvane's catalogue watermark.
reports.postmortemNote: Bait.

reveal.tell: It offers model CX-2, and the photo is from Corvane's catalogue.

crossCheck.text: Corvane shipped CX-4 (R-1-01). Whoever wrote the listing had never seen the crates. For one point, the listing check (C-11) adds that CX-2 went out of production six years ago and the seller account was two days old.

reveal.motive: A theft for resale is an ordinary crime in Halsk, and an ordinary crime doesn't send anyone to look at Brask.

reports.text: Elsin's defence ministry confirms a delay to "a communications upgrade." The opposition asks why secure equipment was routed through a foreign free port.
reports.postmortemNote: The political cost of the delay, which is what made everyone want it over.

reports.text: Marrat customs has opened a routine discrepancy file. Officers searched all nine bonded sheds yesterday and did not find the container.
reports.postmortemNote: The one to remember. Customs searched all nine sheds on the 3rd. On Day 4 the container was "found" in shed 9.

reports.text: The toner has arrived. It is the wrong toner.
reports.postmortemNote: The wrong toner.

reports.text: Maren Lys reappeared on tracking at 0500 today, well offshore and inbound for Halsk. It was dark for three days.
reports.postmortemNote: Three days dark, and back the way it went.

reports.text: If the container isn't found by tomorrow, we invoice Elsin under the loss clause and manufacture again: twelve weeks. If it is found, our engineers can commission the units the day they arrive.
reports.postmortemNote: Pressure, honestly applied.

reports.text: Col. Rhun: "Marrat customs tells us privately that Tessaly's owner has debts, and friends in Kordav who have paid them before. We would like this passed to your people."
reports.postmortemNote: WREN was right, for a reason it gave. It looked like Day 1's sneer and wasn't.

reports.text: The grey-market listing has been marked "SOLD. Collected."
reports.postmortemNote: The theft story, closed on schedule.

reveal.tell: Forty military encryptors sold and collected within a day, in a port whose bonded sheds customs had just searched.

crossCheck.text: Customs was in every shed on the 3rd (R-2-04), and the forwarder's coaster was at that moment on its way back (R-3-01).

reveal.motive: To close the theft story before the container reappeared, so the two stories wouldn't have to share a day.

reports.text: The correct toner has been ordered. Delivery is expected via Halsk.
reports.postmortemNote: More toner.

reports.text: The container has been located in bonded shed 9, mis-stowed. Customs seals are intact and the numbers match. It is released for rail to Kalsa tomorrow morning.
reports.postmortemNote: True reporting of a staged discovery. The tell was in what you already had: shed 9 was searched on the 3rd (R-2-04).

reports.text: Statement: "As we said, a labelling error. Tessaly Freight apologises for the inconvenience."
reports.postmortemNote: The last line of the cover story.

reveal.tell: He said 72 hours, and it took 72 hours.

crossCheck.text: Customs searched all nine sheds on the 3rd and found nothing (R-2-04). The container was found in shed 9 (R-4-01).

reveal.motive: The last line of the cover story, delivered with an apology.

reports.text: Our engineer has examined the crates at Halsk. Customs seals intact, our own tamper tape intact, crate count correct. We recommend installation on arrival.
reports.postmortemNote: An honest inspection of the wrong thing. Seals and tape tell you about seals and tape.

reports.text: Elsin's defence minister says he is "delighted" and that the new terminals will be installed on the 8th.
reports.postmortemNote: The deadline.

reports.text: A container of toner has been found in bonded shed 9.
reports.postmortemNote: Toner, in shed 9.

reports.text: The container was loaded on the 0600 rail service. Marrat customs has closed its discrepancy file: "no offence disclosed."
reports.postmortemNote: "No offence disclosed" was true: nobody disclosed one.

reports.text: Col. Rhun: "The ministry installs tomorrow unless your side objects in writing today. Our procurement people are tired of this, and so am I."
reports.postmortemNote: The last chance, and Rhun's patience.

reports.text: A Halsk dockworkers' forum: the night shift at shed 9 was sent home early on the 5th, "and some private crew did the stow. Since when?"
reports.postmortemNote: An F-graded forum post that was exactly right: a night shift sent home, and a private crew in a bonded shed.

reports.text: Our commissioning team is in Kalsa and ready. We would be grateful for confirmation that installation can proceed.
reports.postmortemNote: Corvane wanted to finish the job.

reports.text: The toner is the right toner. The printer has been condemned.
reports.postmortemNote: The printer.

reports.text: Maren Lys is alongside a fenced quay at Brask. One container stands on the quay under a tarpaulin, beside a windowless warehouse with a new roof. Two guards at the gate.
reports.postmortemNote: The container, in Kordav, beside a guarded warehouse.

reports.text: The fenced quay at Brask is empty. The warehouse doors are shut. Maren Lys is not in port.
reports.postmortemNote: Too late: it had been and gone.

reports.text: Halsk bonded area: shed 9's doors stand open in every pass, pallets only. No container with the consignment's markings anywhere.
reports.postmortemNote: Shed 9 was empty. This is what broke Day 4's good news.

reports.text: Halsk bonded area: one container with the consignment's markings in shed 9.
reports.postmortemNote: It was there by then.

reports.text: Maren Lys has made the same run twice before: Halsk to Brask and back with its transponder off, each time inside four days. Its owner of record is a holding company with an address in Kordav.
reports.postmortemNote: The coaster's pattern, and its owner.

reports.text: Halsk port police visited Tessaly's office and sheds 4 and 6 this morning at Kalsa's request. The staff had the paperwork laid out before the officers arrived. Nothing found.
reports.postmortemNote: The request went to Kalsa and on to Halsk, and Tessaly knew before the police did.

reports.text: Tessaly's owner to an unidentified man: "Thirty-six hours, same as before. It goes back the way it came, same shed fee." The other man: "Seals?" "My man has the pliers and the numbers."
reports.postmortemNote: The whole operation in four lines.

reports.text: Tessaly's office line is quiet. One call: staff are told to "use the other phones this week."
reports.postmortemNote: What you got after the port police called. They had been warned.

reports.text: GANNET: a container left shed 6 on the night of the 1st on a Tessaly truck. It went to the coaster berth, not to the rail siding. The gate log was written up afterwards.
reports.postmortemNote: How it left, and that the gate log was false.

pin.label: Left by truck, night of the 1st

reports.text: GANNET: the container came back on the night of the 5th. A private crew stowed it in shed 9 and one of them was closing seals with a hand tool. He has never seen customs seals put on at night.
reports.postmortemNote: How it came back, and who sealed it.

reports.text: Tessaly has handled one earlier consignment for Corvane Systems: four years ago, the original terminal hardware for Elsin's defence ministry. Port logs show it sat in Halsk a day and a half longer than booked.
reports.postmortemNote: The same forwarder, the same port and the same day and a half, four years ago.

reports.text: The grey-market seller account was created the day the loss became public. The model listed, CX-2, has been out of production for six years. Corvane shipped CX-4.
reports.postmortemNote: The listing was bait.

reports.text: A voice at the Brask warehouse, to an unidentified office: "Forty of forty done. Closing up."
reports.postmortemNote: Something was done to every unit.

tellLabels.agenda-aligned: Lines up with the reporter's own agenda
tellLabels.wrong-model: A detail that doesn't match the consignment
tellLabels.catalogue-photo: A stock photo, not the goods

endings.title: Sent back
endings.text: The crates go back to Corvane unopened. Their engineers are offended. Six weeks later an independent lab opens one, and Corvane's chairman flies to Kalsa in person.

endings.title: Passed
endings.text: Corvane's engineers inspect seals, tape and serial numbers for three weeks and find nothing wrong, because nothing is wrong with the seals, the tape or the serial numbers. The terminals are installed in the new year.

endings.title: Installed
endings.text: The terminals are in the ministry's communications room by the evening of the 8th. The minister is photographed with one.

dailyUpdates.text: A container of secure communications hardware for Elsin's defence ministry is two days overdue at Halsk.
Elsin's ministry has confirmed the delay in public.
Corvane has given notice that it will invoke the contract's loss clause tomorrow.
The container has been found at Halsk.
The container left Halsk by rail at 0600 and reaches Kalsa tonight.

script.text: A container vanished, and the forwarder's own ship left that night with its lights off. The port's records said shed 6. The records were written afterwards.
Tessaly's owner said it would take 72 hours to find. A listing appeared offering the wrong model with a catalogue photo. Both were meant to keep you looking at Halsk.
Rhun, who had sneered on Day 1, passed on something true. The ship turned for home.
The container was found in a shed that customs had searched three days earlier. Its seals were perfect. Everyone who told you so was telling the truth as they knew it.
A dockworkers' forum asked why the night shift had been sent home. Nobody else did.

lessons: When something lost comes back, ask where it has been, not whether it's all there.
A seal tells you about the seal.
Honest people can carry a false story further than a liar can.
A source that sneers and a source that reports can be the same source on different days. Read the item.
How you ask is part of what you learn. Some questions warn the people you're asking about.

missedCollection.1: Imagery of the Brask waterfront: the container was sitting on a quay in Kordav.
missedCollection.2: Tessaly's office (SIGINT), unless the port police had already called there.
missedCollection.3: The warehouse at Brask (SIGINT): the work was finished that day.
missedCollection.4: GANNET, or imagery of the Halsk sheds from earlier in the week: either shows shed 9 was empty until last night.
missedCollection.5: Nothing tasked today could arrive in time.

postmortem.openQuestion: Four years ago the same forwarder handled the ministry's original terminals, and they too spent an extra day and a half in Halsk. And if you asked Kalsa to have the port police look at Tessaly, Tessaly's staff were ready for them.

pirs.question: What has been done to it?

targets.name: A port-police check on Tessaly, requested through Kalsa
targets.fallback: Kalsa passed the request on. Halsk port police report nothing further.

collection.note: Liaison requests go to Kalsa over LATTICE, and Kalsa passes them on.

burnRules.text: GANNET wasn't at the gate. His shift has been changed.
burnRules.postmortem: GANNET was tasked two days running. A foreman who keeps stepping away from the gate gets his shift changed.

levels.label: Trusted
levels.text: She acts on your confidence as given, with your full collection budget.

levels.label: Questioned
levels.text: Her office trims your collection: 1 point less a day.

levels.label: Discounted
levels.text: 2 points less a day, and she treats your confidence as one step lower: High gets the hold, Medium gets nothing.

triggers.rule: An accusation she made on your word is rebuffed
triggers.note: Credibility −2. She accused a neighbour's port on your word, with nothing to show for it.

triggers.rule: She has to take back what she told Kalsa on your word
triggers.note: Credibility −1. "I've withdrawn what I told Kalsa. Their minister is beginning to keep a list."

triggers.rule: Low confidence two days running (each further Low day too)
triggers.note: Credibility −1. Low again. "If I wanted maybe, I'd read the newspapers."

credibility.summary: Marlowe can't see whether you're right until it's over, and this time perhaps not even then. She can see when she has to take something back, and when you won't commit.

caseFile.text: You kept the replacement terminals out of the ministry.
You found that the ministry's original terminals spent the same extra day and a half in Halsk, four years ago, with the same forwarder.
You asked Kalsa for a port-police check, and afterwards Tessaly's phones had gone quiet. They were ready for the police, and for you.

analysts.name: Imre Vasko
analysts.reveal: Anchors on his first theory. His was that Halsk is Halsk: first a lost container, then a theft, then a lost container again. He dismissed Rhun when she was right. His last note was the only one that looked at what was in front of him.

analysts.name: Noor Halden
analysts.reveal: Slow but careful. Never wrong. Her note on the seals arrived on the morning of the last brief.

analysts.name: Tess Marrow
analysts.reveal: Overconfident. Half right on Day 1, sharp on the listing and in open disagreement with Vasko, and flatly wrong on Day 4.

notes.text: Halsk loses a container a week and finds most of them. I wouldn't panic yet.
No manifest and lights out is smuggling, plain and simple. Cigarettes, usually.
There it is, for sale. Tessaly moves anything for anyone. A grey-market job.
Catalogue photo, and the account looks new. This listing is bait.
Transponders fail. They don't usually fail at ten past two in the morning, just outside the port limit.
Rhun's desk again, with gossip about debts. She'd say the same about any firm in Marrat.
notes.why: This time she had a reason, and gave it.

notes.text: Found in the wrong shed. I did say: Halsk.
notes.why: Customs had searched that shed three days earlier.

notes.text: Seals intact, numbers match, customs happy. Case closed, I'd say.
notes.why: Her flat wrong call of the scenario.

notes.text: Three days dark. Long enough to reach Brask, wait a day and a half, and come back.
Night shift sent home, and a private crew in a bonded shed? In Halsk even the thieves work days. That's odd.
notes.why: The one note where he looked at what was in front of him.

notes.text: An intact seal tells you about the seal.
notes.why: It arrived on the morning of the last brief.

map.title: Schematic of Halsk, Brask and the line to Kalsa
map.caption: Two ports and a railway, not to scale. Reporting will be plotted here as it arrives.
map.truthNote: Red diamonds are where the consignment really was, and what was being done, on Day {day}.
map.legend: Plots reporting as it arrives, not confirmed fact. Dashed pins are items you doubted. Dashed rings are today's taskings.
